description: "How the api/ CLI is published to npm - now `restless` (renamed from @restlessai/cli), bin `restless`, invoked as `npx restless` (the `npx api` dispatcher reaches it for `debug` only), burned version numbers"

The `api/` sub-repo (restlesshq/npx-api) publishes to npm as **`restless`** (unscoped) as of 2026-08-17, renamed from `@restlessai/cli` once the name was acquired. Owners: `gkoberger`, `mjcuva`. **The GitHub repo has been renamed `restlesshq/npx-api` -> `restlesshq/onboarding`** (seen 2026-08-31): the git remote still reads `npx-api` and redirects fine, but `gh` resolves and prints the new name, so PR URLs come back as `restlesshq/onboarding/pull/N`. The install repo's CLAUDE.md still says `npx-api`. Bin is `restless`, entry file `bin/restless.js`. First release under the new name is 0.7.0, continuing the old version line; 0.8.0 followed on 2026-08-31 (the `context` command plus the `skill` removal). Legacy names left live and NOT deprecated: `@restlessai/cli` (0.6.0) and `api-beta` (0.2.0).

**Burned version numbers on `restless`:** `0.0.1`-`0.0.11`, `0.1.2`, `2.0.1`, from the unrelated 2012 package (Cooper Runyan, "A CLI-based http client") that used to own the name. npm never allows a published-then-unpublished version to be reused, so 2.x must skip 2.0.1. Its `0.0.0` is still live and stays in the version list unless npm support removes it.

**The bin file name matters, not just the bin key.** `CLI_NAME` in `lib/config.js` is `path.basename(argv[1])`. A POSIX `.bin/` shim is a symlink so argv[1] is the shim path, but Windows `.cmd` shims invoke the real file path - so `bin/api.js` would have kept printing `npx api ...` on Windows after the rename. Keep the file named after the bin. Also keep exactly ONE bin entry: npm runs a sole bin regardless of its name, which is what makes bare `npx restless` and the dispatcher's sub-npx both work.

**The canonical invocation is `npx restless`, not `npx api`.** Do not tell users, docs or prompts to reach the CLI through the dispatcher: it is out of date and covers almost nothing.

**Dispatcher state (verified against the published tarball 2026-08-31).** ReadMe's `api` package can dispatch to the Restless CLI, and `api@7.0.2` (published 2026-08-18, current `latest`) ships `dist/router.js` spawning `npx -y restless@latest`. The old-name problem is FIXED - it no longer points at `@restlessai/cli`. What replaced it is a narrower problem: routing inverted from an inverse allowlist to an explicit one, `const RESTLESS_COMMANDS = new Set(['debug'])`. Only `debug` is dispatched; every other first non-flag argument (plus `--help`/`-h`/`--version`/`-V` ahead of any command, and bare no-command invocations) falls through to readmeio/api's own Commander program (`'codegen'`). So `npx api debug <id>` reaches the Restless CLI and `npx api init`, `npx api update` and `npx api context` do not.

**This inverts the old note here: a new CLI command now DOES need a dispatcher change** to be reachable via `npx api`, because it must be added to `RESTLESS_COMMANDS`. The previous inverse-allowlist behaviour (everything spawned out except `install`/`list`/`uninstall`) was `api@7.0.0` and is gone. It still pins `@latest` from the registry, so local unpublished builds can't be tested through it without editing the spawn spec. Dispatcher source: readmeio/api (local clone `/Users/marc/Developer/ReadMe/api`), `packages/api/src/router.ts` + `src/bin.ts`; that clone was last seen on `db3d980`, which predates the `RESTLESS_COMMANDS` change, so read the published tarball rather than the clone to check current behaviour.

Because the CLI can still be invoked under more than one name, never hardcode it in user-facing strings: use `CLI_NAME`, or the `cli`/`cliName` params on `fixContext`, `unsupportedStackMessage`, `buildAgentPlan` (all default to `restless`).

Publishing: Marc's npm user is `mjcuva`, 2FA on publish (needs `--otp`). Marc runs `npm publish` himself via `!` bash-input (2FA). `gh pr merge` worked from Claude when Marc explicitly asked (0.9.3, 2026-09-22); earlier it was blocked by the permission classifier. New-package registry propagation took ~2.5 min before `npm view` resolved. An expired npm token makes `npm publish` fail with `E404 Not Found - PUT ...` (npm masks auth failures as 404); diagnose with `npm whoami` (returns E401), fix with `npm login`. Version-bump flow matching repo history: branch, `npm version minor --no-git-tag-version`, PR, merge, publish from main. **A repository ruleset blocks force-pushes to every branch** (`GH013 ... Cannot force-push to this branch`), so once a release branch is pushed you cannot amend or rebase it - stack a follow-up commit instead. Rules: https://github.com/restlesshq/onboarding/rules

Related: [[published-shrinkwrap-is-not-honored]], [[npx-api-lockfile-is-mac-only]], [[cli-nextjs-plugin-integration]]

name: release-prs-stay-scoped-to-the-bump
description: "A release PR contains the version bump and nothing else - don't retrofit docs that a previous PR left out"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

On the 0.8.0 release PR for the `restless` CLI, I noticed the `context` command
had shipped in #34 with no README coverage and added the docs to the release
PR. Marc: "Don't update the readme in this pr. If it wasn't included in the
orignal change we shouldn't do it."

**Why:** a release PR is the version bump. Work that belongs to a different
change stays with that change, so the release stays reviewable as exactly one
thing and the doc gap is attributed to the PR that created it rather than
quietly absorbed into an unrelated one.

**How to apply:** when prepping a release, bump the version and stop. If a
shipped change is missing docs, say so and offer it as its own PR rather than
folding it in. This does not override the repo-wide rule that docs land with
the change that needs them - it decides WHICH PR that is, and it is never the
release PR.

Related: [[npm-publishing-restlessai-cli]]

RES-15 is `npx restless feedback <request-id>`, the CLI half of RES-13. The CLI half was implemented on 2026-10-21 in `lib/feedback.js` (worktree branch investigate-implement-res-15-5c1a13fa). Decisions Marc made when asked:

- An agent run with no `--message` fails with one line and exit 1. It does not read stdin.
- A human at a terminal is asked for a contact email, prefilled from git, Enter confirms, blank sends none.
- Scope was "CLI only": the `api` package half (add `'feedback'` to `RESTLESS_COMMANDS` in readmeio/api `packages/api/src/router.ts`) and both publishes were left for later. The local `~/Developer/ReadMe/api` checkout is stale and lacks router.ts; use GitHub.

The server route `POST /api/logs/<id>/feedback` only exists on restlesshq/app PR #392 (branch res-13-support-planning-9362b80f), unmerged at the time. Prod returned HTTP 200 HTML for it, so the CLI's "unexpected response" fallback fires until that merges.

**Why:** the ticket left both behaviours open, and the router change lives in a different repo with its own publish.
**How to apply:** when picking RES-15 back up, do the readmeio/api router PR and publish `restless` first, `api` second (until `api` is published, `npx api feedback` routes to the codegen CLI). Related: [[release-prs-stay-scoped-to-the-bump]], [[npm-publishing-restlessai-cli]].

I bumped the package to 0.10.1 and opened the release PR: https://github.com/restlesshq/onboarding/pull/61

- **Why a patch:** the only change since 0.10.0 is #60, which polishes the `feedback` command (a spinner while it posts, a prompt when interactive mode is forced, and an "Your email" prompt). There's no new command, so it doesn't need a minor bump.
- **What's in the PR:** just the version change in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, on branch `release/0.10.1`, the same way 0.10.0 was done. The untracked `.claude/` folder isn't included.

Once it's merged, publish from `main`:

```
! git checkout main && git pull && npm publish --otp=<code>
```

I can merge it for you if you'd like.

The `api` package still only forwards `debug` to this CLI, so `npx api feedback` won't work until `feedback` is added to its router. `npx restless feedback` works once this is published.
